summary: Over-engineering analysis across 47 crates, 372,191 lines, 1,321 files

top_10_overengineered.primary_issue: Entire 5,418-line crate (including 2,700 test lines) is unused in production — engine crate has a forked, enhanced copy internally. Only ModelCallParams and QueryDeps trait are imported from outside.
Textbook YAGNI: full AudioCaptureBackend trait hierarchy, feasibility checker, state machine — only production implementation is NullAudioBackend returning 'not available'.
4 of 9 modules are pure re-export stubs (sink.rs: 3 lines, transport.rs: 6 lines, event_class.rs: 5 lines, sdk_mapping.rs: 6 lines).
Single 275-line file as a crate, ~130 lines real logic (6 small conversion functions) + 140 lines tests.

4,172-line shell command parser: tree-sitter AST parser (50K node budget), 1,050-line heredoc parser, 553-line pipe handler — for parsing 'echo hello > file.txt'. sandbox crate has duplicate inline parser.
Zero-dependency crate with only static data tables (model aliases, pricing, mapping) and simple lookup functions. Exists solely due to dependency graph ordering constraints.
9 of 12 ProcessState fields are dead code. Signal<T> unused. model.rs is a one-line re-export no production code imports.
Single-consumer crate with IpcTransport/Reader/Writer traits for only 2 implementations, one of which (MemoryTransport) is test-only.
408-line macro system generating 5+ enums. 19 extremely fragmented v1 modules (capabilities.rs: 12 lines, health.rs: 12 lines). ServerNotification is an empty enum.

32K-line monolith: forked query loop (952 lines), god-objects (QueryEngineState ~20 concerns, AppState ~22 fields), AgentRuntimeAdapters service locator with 6+ Arc<dyn Trait> fields in global OnceLock.

architectural_concerns: Forked query loop: allthecodes-query (~5,418 lines) entirely unused in production; engine maintains internal forked copy with added features
Quadruple config representation: RawSettings, EffectiveSettings, SettingsJson, and JSON Schema duplicate ~80+ settings fields
Global static service locator pattern: 5+ crates use LazyLock/OnceLock<RwLock<...>> as process-global registries
IPC protocol dualism: v1 (BackendMessage/FrontendMessage) and v2 (IpcPayload with envelopes) coexist
Daemon dual storage backends: every write persists to both SQLite and JSON files
Workspace split artifacts: 10-12 crates extracted during Phase 4/7 reorganization, boundaries never justified
allthecodes-commands depends on 24/40 workspace crates — compilation bottleneck
result.final_verdict: The project has a clear split into legitimate crates (engine, daemon, tools, config, permissions, session, types, api — justified by multiple consumers or domain complexity) and workspace split artifacts (Phase 4/7 reorganization). IPC family is most egregious: 4 extra crates ~6,300 lines where 1 crate would serve. YAGNI violations account for ~2,000 lines of unused code. Forked query loop is the most expensive single issue. Recommended: merge 6 highest-score crates, eliminate ~7 crates and ~9,000 lines of dead/ceremonial code, then address config quadruple representation and global service locators.
